earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog yang1289 lists only classification works (Bennett 1983; Boyd & Pasch 1988; Hackett & van Bulck 1956); no description of Yango found

sources.note: Ethnographic; only lists 'Mabo, Monzombo, Kpala, Oyango' as related peoples of the Bozene. Nothing linguistic on Yango.

sources.citation: Calloc'h, J. 1911. Vocabulaire francais-gmbwaga-gbanziri-monjombo, precede d'elements de grammaire. Paris: Geuthner.
sources.note: Covers Ngbaka Ma'bo, Gbanziri and Monzombo jointly ('Accent tonique' p. 8); Yango is not among the varieties treated and is never named.

sources.citation: Ebanda wa Kalema. 1991. Le kpala, un parler oubanguien. Annales Aequatoria 12: 321-330.
sources.note: Describes KPALA (Libenge variety), Yango's closest relative, not Yango: tones H/M/L plus rising and falling (sec. 2 'Phonemes supra-segmentaires', p. 328); no mention of accent or stress anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Kamanda Kola. 1990. Inventaire des langues et/ou dialectes oubanguiens du Zaire. Annales Aequatoria 11: 165-187 (whole volume fetched sources).
sources.note: Nothing. Yango has no entry of its own; under 2.7 Gbanziri (p. 172) the author says Van Bulck attaches Yango to Gbanziri and that 'on ne dispose d'aucun document adequat' on it, i.e. no description existed as of 1990.

sources.citation: Ebanda wa Kalema. (announced 1990) Esquisse phonologique et morphologique du kpala: un parler oubanguien. GRELOUBA, 'en preparation' (cited in Kamanda 1990: 173).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: If it was ever completed it would be the fullest description of the Kpala-Yango cluster; existence unverified.

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Gent / Universite Libre de Bruxelles.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Recent fieldwork in exactly the Libenge/Kungu area with a chapter on Bantu-Ubangian contact; may contain first-hand phonological notes or wordlists for Yango/Kpala.

sources.citation: Donzo, Jean-Pierre. 2007. Etude comparee du vocabulaire culturel dans quelques langues ubangiennes du nord-ouest de la RDC: une perspective ethnolinguistique. Memoire de DEA/licence, Universite de Kinshasa. 235 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only Glottolog reference with Yango data beyond a name (c. 20 pp.); a transcription-conventions section might state tone/accent marking for Yango.

sources.citation: Monino, Yves (ed.). 1988. Lexique comparatif des langues oubanguiennes. Paris: Geuthner (incl. R. Boyd, 'Le groupe sere-ngbaka-mba').
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Comparative wordlists with short phonological notes per language for the Sere-Ngbaka-Mba group; if Yango or Kpala is among the varieties, the notes may state tone inventory and absence/presence of accent.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI (ch. on the Sere-Mundu / Ngbaka Ma'bo group, sec. 2 'Tone and Stress').

sources.note: Group-level tone-and-stress remarks for the Ngbaka-Ma'bo/Monzombo/Kpala/Yango cluster; would at best give a second-hand family-level statement, not a Yango-specific one.

sources.citation: Hackett, Peter & Gaston van Bulck. 1956. Report of the Eastern Team: Oubangi to Great Lakes. In M. Guthrie & A. N. Tucker (eds), Linguistic Survey of the Northern Bantu Borderland, vol. 1, 63-122. London: OUP for the International African Institute.

sources.note: The only fieldwork-based publication Glottolog links to Yango (van Bulck is the one who attached Yango to Gbanziri); the team's notes sometimes include remarks on tone/stress per language. Only ~2 pp. concern Yango, so expectations are low.
